title: What reviewers and the City Attorney found
question: What have auditors, reviewers and enforcement offices put in writing about how these drawings, lists, grant rounds and pools were run, and about cheating in them?
finding: 19 passages from audits, reviews and enforcement releases are on disk, 5 of them about below-market-rate housing. On housing, the City Attorney reported in December 2018: “City enforcement has so far returned 21 homes to their intended purpose — providing affordable housing to San Franciscans who need it”. On grants, the Controller’s 2023 review of the Community Challenge Grant round found 4 separate failures in how applications were scored. No review of the condominium-conversion lottery’s drawings was found; what is on disk about it is the program’s own status reports.
how: Every row of the download’s rules-and-reviews table whose kind is a review, audit, enforcement release or litigation notice, quoted as the table quotes it (25 words at most), plus short passages read directly from two documents in this project’s library: the Controller’s review of the 2023 grant round and the Budget and Legislative Analyst’s report on vacant below-market-rate rentals. Each quotation was checked against the saved text.
limits: These are the authorities’ words, and several are allegations in lawsuits or press releases at the time of filing, not judgments; people named in those documents are not named here. The housing enforcement releases describe buyers alleged to have lied to obtain a below-market-rate home or to have rented it out afterwards; none describes a fault in how a drawing was run. The search of the City Attorney’s site was by keyword and will have missed releases worded differently. The Controller’s cannabis-permit report could not be fetched.
